newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OMV to up gas pipeline capacity by 50 pc.
newsitem.headline: OMV to up gas pipeline capacity by 50 pc.

text.p: Austrian oil and chemicals group OMV AG aims to boost its gas pipeline capacity by half next year, raising gas revenues by 15-20 percent, exploration and production director Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer said on Monday.
Austria, bordered by former communist states to the east and EU nations to the west, is a main artery for Russian gas exports to western Europe.
In the first nine-months gas, the powerhouse of OMV's business, posted steady 1.29 billion schillings earnings before interest and tax.

"By the middle of 1997 we will increase our gas pipeline capacity to 30 billion cubic metres from 20 billion cubic metres...That should lead to a 15-20 percent increase in gas revenues next year," Ruttenstorfer told Reuters in an interview.
He saw little threat from other operators offering similar gas transit facilities in central Europe. "Our protection is in our cost position. It is the best one can hope to achieve."

OMV was in talks with neighbouring countries interested in storing strategic gas requirements in Austria, Ruttenstorfer revealed. He said a decision on expanding OMV's gas storage would be taken if and when deals were signed.
Ruttenstorfer reiterated that OMV was interested in buying into a regional gas supplier, like Burgenland firm BEGAS.
